input.quote: unless either party notifies the other party in writing at least ninety (90) days prior to the end of the then-current term for the applicable Service Option Attachment that it has elected to terminate such Service Option Attachment.
input.rationale: § 3.2 renews each Service Option Attachment automatically unless notice is given at least ninety (90) days before the end of the then-current term. That 90-day window exceeds the fallback ceiling of a 60-day non-renewal notice window (and is well short of our preferred 30-day opt-out with a 60-day vendor reminder), so it is a deviation. The edit shortens the window to sixty (60) days and states in operative text that Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days. The renewal clause permits no uplift — renewal is for a term equal in duration to the previous term on the existing terms — so the 5% price-cap element is not engaged; IBM's separate unilateral price-change right in § 13.1 (only after 12 months, on 90 days' notice, with a fee-free Customer exit) is a change-of-terms mechanic and is not double-flagged here. Renewal-term length mirroring the previous term is a preferred-level point noted rather than redlined; if any Service Option Attachment term exceeds 12 months we would escalate and fix the renewal term at 12 months.

ops.text: Customer's non-renewal notice window under this Section 3.2 is no more than 60 days.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We have cut the automatic-renewal notice window from ninety (90) days to sixty (60) days and confirmed that Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days, so an early deadline cannot lock us into a further renewal term; 60 days is our fallback (preferred is a 30-day opt-out with a 60-day reminder).
proposal.summary: Set the § 3.2 non-renewal notice window at no more than 60 days.

mappings.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
